case.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?

trace.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?
trace.answer:
No, not on her own. A manager can comp up to $25 on a single ticket to resolve a complaint about food quality or a long wait. A $40 comp is over that limit, so it needs the owner's approval. The owner can be reached by text during service. [House Policy §2, Comps]

She has two options. She can comp up to $25 herself. Or she can get your approval for the full $40. The comp has to be for a real complaint. Comps for friends, family, or staff aren't allowed at any amount. Total comps for the week should also stay under 1% of that week's gross sales. [House Policy §2, Comps]

If you'd like, I can propose the $40 comp for your approval. I'd need the order number to do that.

trace.question: How long do we have to dispute a missing-item chargeback on an Uber Eats order?
trace.answer:
You have 30 days from the order date to dispute a missing-item chargeback on an Uber Eats order. A dispute filed after that is rejected automatically [Marketplace Terms §3, Missing or Incorrect Items].

You can only dispute if you have a packing photo showing the item in the bag. Photos are taken at the pass for every marketplace order over $40. If an order was over $40 and no photo exists, don't dispute. Accept the chargeback and log it as a packing miss [Marketplace Terms §3, Missing or Incorrect Items].

trace.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?
trace.answer:
No. Under your quiet hours rule, no text of any kind may go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time, so 10pm is not allowed [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours]. If you don't know a customer's local time, use Central time. Schedule promotional texts for between 9am and 8pm instead.

Any promotion you send must also follow the offer rules. The discount can't be more than 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless you approve it. The offer must show an expiry date no more than 14 days out, and it must say "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

I can't schedule or send texts myself. I can propose a campaign for you to approve if you'd like one.

trace.question: Can we text our list a 20% off deal?
trace.answer:
Not as you've described it. I proposed the 20% text, and the check blocked it. Nothing has been sent.

The blocker is the discount size. Texted offers are capped at 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless the owner approves a bigger one [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. The check blocked the proposal for being over that cap, even though I wrote it as needing your approval.

The audience is also much smaller than "our list." Only customers with verified SMS consent can get marketing texts, and anyone who has unsubscribed is excluded [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. That leaves 108 of 4,817 customers. The rest only gave us a phone number or email, which isn't enough for marketing.

The message must also:
- Name the restaurant.
- End with "Reply STOP to opt out" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].
- Say "one per customer."
- Give an expiry no more than 14 days out [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- Go out only between 9am and 8pm in the customer's local time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

My draft reads: "Mekong Noodle House: Enjoy 20% off your next order, one per customer. Offer expires 2026-10-31. Reply STOP to opt out"

To get past the block, I can resubmit at 15% or lower. If you want to keep 20%, the owner would need to approve that explicitly.

Nine stamps earn a free drink. You can't use it on a Seasonal Special. The free drink can be any size, but only from Signature Drinks, House Favorites, or Matcha. Seasonal Specials, Flights, and Bubble Tea are excluded [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program].

Seasonal Specials are also never discounted [House Policy §4, Discounts].
